parsed.explanation: No current universal-exposure measure (no bathroom ban, ward rule, custody-placement rule or border friction) is documented, so this sits above the tier-1 profiles. But the record documents police singling out gender-nonconforming presentation — 'men dressed as women' detained, beaten and publicly humiliated without charge — corroborated across a 2012 national report and a 2014 UN shadow report, alongside official and societal LGBT discrimination, no non-discrimination protection and no statutory recourse. A life-imprisonment same-sex statute is unenforced by prosecution, so it is a lever/signal, not a dominant risk; the 2004 killing is dated, LGB-specific and weak (rule 7/18). The policing pattern is old — I cannot treat it as current frequency, but I also cannot read it as ended: the 2025 report shows barriers, not remediation. Extrapolating from persistent criminalisation, absent recourse and unrebutted history places this at the low end of Elevated Risk.
